a DCF values a company based on the cash it will produce in the future. first i project unlevered free cash flow for five to ten years, which is EBIT times one minus the tax rate, plus D&A, minus capex, minus the increase in working capital. second i pick a discount rate, usually WACC, which blends the cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt at the target capital structure. third, since the company keeps going after the forecast, i calculate a terminal value, either with the Gordon growth method using a perpetual growth rate near long-term GDP, or with an exit multiple on final year EBITDA. fourth i discount each year's cash flow and the terminal value back to today at WACC and add them up, which gives enterprise value. last, to get equity value i subtract debt and preferred and noncontrolling interest and add cash, then divide by diluted shares to get an implied share price, which i compare to the current price.
